Brandan Keith Wright was born on October 5, 1987.
Brandan Keith Wright is an American former professional basketball player.
Wright fast became a standout at his high school Brentwood Academy.
Wright earned three "Mr. Basketball" titles in Tennessee.
Wright led his high school team to four consecutive state championships.
Wright was eventually recruited by the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill's basketball team.
In his lone season as a Tar Heel, Wright was named the Atlantic Coast Conference Rookie of the Year.
In his lone season as a Tar Heel, Wright earned All-ACC Second Team honors.
In the 2007 NBA draft, Wright was chosen eighth overall by the Charlotte Bobcats.
Wright was then dealt to the Golden State Warriors for guard Jason Richardson in a draft-night trade.
Wright was born and raised in Nashville, Tennessee.
Wright became a two-time first-team Parade All-American selection at Brentwood Academy.
As a senior, Wright averaged 22.4 points per contest.
As a senior, Wright averaged 9.4 rebounds per contest.
As a senior, Wright averaged 5.1 blocks per contest.
As a senior, Wright recorded four triple-doubles (points, rebounds, assists).
Wright earned Tennessee's Division II Mr. Basketball title in 2004.
Wright earned Tennessee's Division II Mr. Basketball title in 2005.
Wright earned Tennessee's Division II Mr. Basketball title in 2006.
Wright led his Brentwood Academy team to four consecutive state titles, a first in Tennessee high school basketball history.
Considered a five-star recruit by Rivals.com, Wright was listed as the No. 1 power forward and the No. 3 player in the nation in 2006.
Wright appeared in thirty-seven games in his lone season at the University of North Carolina.
Wright started all thirty-seven games he played during his lone season at the University of North Carolina.
Wright averaged 14.7 points per game on 64.6% field goal shooting during his lone season at the University of North Carolina.
Wright's .646 field goal percentage led the Atlantic Coast Conference (ACC) and was the best ever by an ACC freshman.
Wright led the North Carolina team in blocks with sixty-five, sixth in the ACC.
Wright finished second on the team in scoring with 14.7 points per game, thirteenth in the ACC.
Wright finished second on the team in rebounding with 6.2 rebounds per game, fourteenth in the ACC.
Wright scored 20-or-more points on eight occasions during his lone season at the University of North Carolina.
Wright was named to the NCAA All-East Regional Team after averaging 12.8 points and 7.0 rebounds in four Tournament contests.
Wright was named MVP of the ACC Tournament, becoming just the fifth freshman in conference history to win the award.
Wright was also named Atlantic Coast Conference Rookie of the Year (the third straight Tar Heel to earn the honor).
Wright earned All-ACC Second Team honors during his lone season at the University of North Carolina.
Due to an injured hip flexor, Wright was unable to participate in summer league play during his rookie season with the Golden State Warriors.
Of the thirty-eight games Wright played during his rookie season, he started in six.
Wright entered the 2008–09 season with career averages of 4.0 points and 2.6 rebounds in 9.9 minutes over thirty-eight games in his rookie season.
In January 2009, Wright partially dislocated his left shoulder late in the first half of a game against the Los Angeles Lakers.
On October 14, 2009, the Warriors extended Wright's contract until the end of the 2010–11 NBA season.
Wright damaged his left shoulder capsule during practice on October 2, 2009.
He underwent shoulder surgery and missed the 2009–10 season with the Golden State Warriors.
On February 23, 2011, Wright was traded to the New Jersey Nets along with Dan Gadzuric in exchange for Troy Murphy and a second round pick.
On December 9, 2011, he signed a deal with the Dallas Mavericks.
Wright recorded a career-high seven blocked shots in a win at Houston on March 24, 2012.
He became the eighth player in Mavericks history to record seven blocks in a game and the first since Erick Dampier in 2008.
Wright matched the block total posted by the entire Rockets' team.
Wright averaged 6.9 points, 3.6 rebounds, and 1.3 blocks in 16.1 minutes per game during the 2011–12 NBA season with the Dallas Mavericks.
Wright scored in double figures 13 times during the 2011–12 NBA season with the Dallas Mavericks.
Wright shot a team-high 61.8 percent from the field during the 2011–12 NBA season with the Dallas Mavericks.
Wright made his NBA Playoff debut in Game 1 at Oklahoma City on April 28, 2012.
Wright scored his first career playoff point on a free throw attempt in Game 2 against the Thunder.
On July 25, 2013, Wright re-signed with the Dallas Mavericks.
On December 18, 2014, Wright was traded, along with Jameer Nelson and Jae Crowder, to the Boston Celtics in exchange for Rajon Rondo and Dwight Powell.
On January 9, 2015, Wright was traded to the Phoenix Suns in exchange for a protected 2015 first-round pick via the Minnesota Timberwolves.
Wright scored 16 points, grabbed 8 rebounds, and tied a career-high 7 blocks while starting in a close 74–72 victory over the New Orleans Pelicans on January 9, 2015.
On July 9, 2015, Wright signed a three-year, $17.1 million contract with the Memphis Grizzlies.
Wright injured his right knee on November 7, 2015, and missed the rest of the 2015–16 season bar a five-game stint in February.
Wright returned to the Grizzlies' lineup during the 2016 preseason but was sidelined for the start of the 2016–17 season due to an ankle injury.
On November 16, 2016, Wright underwent a successful arthroscopic debridement of his left ankle after non-surgical interventions failed to eliminate his posterior tibialis tendinopathy.
He was subsequently ruled out for two months and made his season debut on January 30, 2017, against the Phoenix Suns.
Wright missed the majority of December 2017 with a groin injury.
On February 10, 2018, Wright was waived by the Memphis Grizzlies.
On February 12, 2018, Wright signed with the Houston Rockets.
On March 23, 2018, Wright was waived by the Houston Rockets.
Growing up, Wright's favorite player was Kevin Garnett.
Wright is a fan of Chris Bosh's game and models some of his playing style from the two.
Wright is considered to be a superior finisher from within twelve feet and especially at the rim.
Wright's biggest weakness seemed to be his strength, as well as his sporadic defensive efforts.
Wright has two younger brothers named Brian and Trevor.
Brian played basketball at Lipscomb University in Nashville from 2007 to 2011.
Wright has participated in various community outreach projects associated with the Golden State Warriors.
Wright enjoys bowling, fishing, golfing, and playing video games.
Wright's favorite actor is Will Smith.
Wright's favorite movie is Bad Boys II.
Wright was a pitcher when he played baseball in his youth.
Wright's favorite foods are fried chicken and steak.
Wright's favorite teams in other sports are the Atlanta Braves (MLB), Nashville Predators (NHL), and the Tennessee Titans (NFL).
Wright wears a size fourteen shoe.
